title: Hamming Distance Problem

notes: The Hamming distance is the number of differing bit positions; leading zeroes do not contribute differences.
Because x and y are non-negative integers below 2^31, at most 31 bit positions need to be considered.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: 1 and 4 differ at two bit positions.
3 is 11 in binary and 1 is 01, so only one position differs.

content.problemStatement:
The [Hamming distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamming_distance) between two integers is the number of positions at which the corresponding bits are different.

With two integers `x` and `y`, output *the **Hamming distance** between them*.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: x = 1, y = 4
Output: 2
Explanation:
1   (0 0 0 1)
4   (0 1 0 0)
       ↑   ↑
The above arrows point to positions where the corresponding bits are different.
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: x = 3, y = 1
Output: 1
```

**Constraints:**

* `0 <= x, y <= 2^31 - 1`

**Note:** This question is the same as  [2220: Smallest Bit Flips to Convert Number.](https://leetcode.com/problems/smallest-bit-flips-to-convert-number/description/)

notes: The solution uses only fixed-width integer bit operations; the maximum Hamming distance is 31 under the stated constraint.
XOR identifies differing bit positions directly. The loop x &= x - 1 removes the lowest set bit each iteration, so the number of loop iterations equals the Hamming distance.
solution.approach: Compute x XOR y. Every set bit in the XOR result marks a position where x and y differ. Count those set bits using Brian Kernighan’s bit-counting method, which clears one set bit per iteration.

better.complexity: O(31) worst-case time and O(1) space.
better.description: First compute z = x XOR y. Then scan the set bits of z one position at a time and count them. This avoids separately comparing the two inputs at every bit position.

optimal.complexity: O(k) time, where k is the number of set bits in x XOR y, with O(1) space.
optimal.description: Compute z = x XOR y and repeatedly clear its lowest set bit with z &= z - 1. Each iteration counts one differing position, so the loop runs exactly once per set bit.

bruteForce.complexity: O(31) time and O(1) space, which is O(1) for this fixed-width constraint.
bruteForce.description: Compare the lowest bit of x and y, count whether they differ, then shift both values right and repeat for all 31 possible bit positions.

solution.timeComplexity: O(k), where k is the number of set bits in x XOR y; k <= 31 under the constraints.
